info.title: Khan Academy API v1 (removed)
info.description: The public Khan Academy REST API v1 (content library, badges and user progress) and its OAuth 1.0a token endpoints, as last documented by Khan Academy before it removed them: /badges, /user and /playlists on 2020-01-06, /topictree, /topic, /videos and /exercises on 2020-07-29 (per the khan-api README). Every /api/v1 route now answers 410 Gone ('API removed'), so this document is historical. The OpenFn khanacademy adaptor's fetch({ getEndpoint, queryParams, postUrl }) runs the auth2 request_token -> authorize (POST with the app owner's email/password) -> access_token dance against https://www.khanacademy.org/api/auth2 and then GETs https://www.khanacademy.org/api/v1/<getEndpoint>; it can no longer succeed.

post.summary: Get an OAuth 1.0a request token (auth flow v2)
post.description: Step 1 of the v2 flow (added March 2015). OAuth parameters are sent signed (HMAC-SHA1); the OpenFn adaptor sends them via the request library's oauth option. Removed with the rest of the public API in 2020 (request_token now answers 404 'API removed.').

401.description: Bad OAuth signature or token.

get.summary: Browser approval page for a request token
get.description: Step 2 (interactive): the user's browser is sent here with oauth_token, logs in and approves; redirects to oauth_callback (or /api/auth/default_callback) with oauth_token, oauth_token_secret and oauth_verifier.

302.description: Redirect to the callback after approval.

post.summary: Approve a request token directly with the app owner's credentials
post.description: Step 2 (non-interactive): only for the KA user who registered the app. The client must follow all redirects. This is what the OpenFn adaptor's fetch() does with configuration.email/password.

get.summary: Exchange an authorised request token for an access token
get.description: Step 3. Signed with the consumer key/secret and the request token/secret; oauth_verifier is required if oauth_callback was given in step 1. Removed with the rest of the public API in 2020 (request_token now answers 404 'API removed.').

401.description: Bad OAuth signature or token.

get.summary: Get a request token (legacy v1 flow)
get.description: Legacy non-standard v1 flow: redirects through the identity-provider login and returns the token on the callback. Removed with the rest of the public API in 2020 (request_token now answers 404 'API removed.').

401.description: Bad OAuth signature or token.

get.summary: Exchange a request token for an access token (legacy v1 flow)
get.description: Legacy v1 flow; identical to the v2 access_token step. Removed with the rest of the public API in 2020 (request_token now answers 404 'API removed.').

401.description: Bad OAuth signature or token.

TopicChild.description: Abbreviated child entry of a topic. `id` is the readable_id for videos, the name for exercises and the id for topics.

Topic.description: A node of the content topic tree.

id.description: Topic slug; 'root' is the root of the tree.

children.description: Children: abbreviated entries on /topic/{id}; full Topic/Video/Exercise objects on /topictree.

extra_properties.description: Type not documented (null in every example).

playlists.description: Titles of playlists containing the video (older responses).

creation_date.description: Timestamp (examples use both with and without a trailing Z).

summative.description: Boolean; one documented example returns the string "false".

user_badges.description: Only present on authenticated calls, when the user has earned the badge.

identifier.description: Username or email of the KA account that registered the app.

Error.description: Plain-text error body. Since 2020 every /api/v1 route answers 410 'API removed. Please see https://github.com/Khan/khan-api for details'.

khanOAuth1.name: Authorization
khanOAuth1.description: OAuth 1.0a (HMAC-SHA1) signed request: consumer key/secret plus access token/secret from /api/auth2/access_token. OpenAPI 3.0 has no native OAuth 1 scheme, so it is modelled as the signed Authorization header.
